summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent lower extremity cellulitis, chronic venous insufficiency, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for acute left leg pain, erythema, and swelling concerning for infection. Initial broad-spectrum antibiotics were given, later narrowed to cefazolin, then re-escalated to IV vancomycin due to worsening erythema. Dermatology and infectious disease confirmed cellulitis. During admission, she developed C. difficile colitis, requiring oral vancomycin. Blood cultures were negative, and ultrasound showed no abscess. She improved clinically, was transitioned to oral linezolid for completion of antibiotic therapy, and was discharged home with plans for infectious disease follow-up, warfarin monitoring, and resumption of home medications including torsemide once diarrhea resolved.
